A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SAQ decoder and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A-G. Content can be matched reliably despite pagination and formatting changes.

before.justification: V1 reports original decoding simulations, logical error rates, thresholds, architectural ablations, recovery-weight comparisons, and computational measurements in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical evaluations in Section 5 and the appendices, including decoding outcomes, ablations, and efficiency measurements.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Appendices A-B retain the same dual-stream transformer, asymmetric attention, global token, three-component loss, and CPND projection/nullspace-descent procedure. Algorithm 1 is unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate toric and rotated surface codes under independent and depolarizing noise, plus color and repetition codes under circuit noise. No code family, noise scenario, or task coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: The corresponding evaluations retain QECCT, MWPM, BPOSD-2, and SAQ without CPND. Appendix B retains the naive-projection and OSD-0 comparisons, and Table 3 retains its threshold comparator set.

E3.justification: Code distances, noise ranges, circuit rounds, evaluation metrics, and model/training configurations remain unchanged in Section 5 and Appendix D/Table 2. The revised efficiency values are not accompanied by a reported protocol change.

E4.justification: Section 5.2 retains the same architecture, weight-sharing, loss-component, and masking/global-token ablations. Appendix B's recovery-weight analysis is unchanged; Figure 7 receives a caption correction rather than a new analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same point-estimate and curve reporting, without reported repeated-run/seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the evaluations.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises SAQ/QECCT FLOPs from 0.21/1.05 to 0.11/0.26 G at L=6 and from 0.80/4.10 to 0.39/0.71 G at L=10, under depolarizing noise. Corresponding inference times change from 1.2/7.0 to 0.06/0.34 ms and from 4.5/20.1 to 0.45/2.3 ms. These are localized summary-table revisions: detailed Table 4, decoding results, thresholds, and method rankings remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, loss derivations, and Propositions A.1, A.2, and B.1 with their proofs are unchanged. Appendix B's paragraph and page-break adjustments do not alter its reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same architectural, loss, and CPND contributions, near-ML toric thresholds of 10.99% and 18.6%, and claims of linear scaling in syndrome size and applicability across stabilizer codes.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 removes the assertion that parameter efficiency directly produces reduced memory footprint, faster training convergence, and improved deployment. Other mechanism explanations and Appendix D's limitation concerning restricted hyperparameter exploration remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix D/Table 2 retain the same hyperparameters, training budgets, epoch times, implementation origins, and 48GB NVIDIA L40S hardware disclosure. The reproducibility statement retains the same stated source-code access information.

R1.justification: The bibliography and research positioning are unchanged, including comparisons with QECCT, AlphaQubit, and CrossMPT. No cited work is added or removed.

P1.justification: V2 makes limited prose cuts in Section 5, adjusts paragraph breaks in Appendix B, and adds the ICLR 2026 publication header. The section order and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 7's caption changes from 'Rotated surface code results' to 'Ablation studies results.' Table 4 regroups repeated code-distance and noise labels and changes separators without changing numerical entries. Reflow brings the full conclusion onto page 10; the figures' plotted content is unchanged.

improvement.justification: V2 brings Table 1's efficiency summary much closer to the unchanged detailed results in Appendix F/Table 4, reducing a substantial internal inconsistency. It also fixes Figure 7's misleading caption and tempers the parameter-efficiency interpretation. These improve consistency and clarity, although the numerical revisions lack an accompanying measurement-protocol explanation and do not establish newly achieved performance gains.
